content5.ptxt: A three-way catalyst is used to efficiently purify CO (carbon monoxide), HC (hydrocarbons) and NOx (nitrogen oxides) in the exhaust gas. As the three-way catalyst functions most efficiently near the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio, CO, HC and NOx cannot be purified efficiently unless the engine is accurately controlled near the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. The oxygen sensor is installed for the purpose of this control. The oxygen sensor uses the characteristic that its output voltage changes suddenly when it detects the oxygen concentration in exhaust gas discharged under normal combustion near the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio, and sends a signal to the engine control computer so that the air-fuel ratio can be controlled accurately.

A zirconia element is used as the sensor element. The inside of the zirconium element is exposed to the outside air and the outside is exposed to the exhaust gas, and it generates a voltage according to the difference in oxygen concentration between the exhaust gas and the outside air. The engine control computer determines whether the air-fuel ratio is rich or lean based on the output voltage of the oxygen sensor, and controls the injection volume accordingly. When the exhaust temperature is low, the sensor cannot generate a useful voltage signal without supplementary heating. Therefore, the oxygen sensor has a heater that warms the zirconia element, and the engine control computer adjusts the heater current using duty ratio control.

item.ptxt: While the vehicle is being driven after the engine has warmed up, the engine control computer performs active air-fuel ratio control for approximately 30 seconds or more. At this time, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition. During this time, deterioration of the three-way catalyst and malfunctions of the oxygen sensor are detected.

During active air-fuel ratio control, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition. If the oxygen sensor malfunctions, the amount of change in its output voltage becomes small.

If the oxygen sensor outputs voltage only between 0.21 V and 0.59 V during active air-fuel ratio control, the engine control computer judges that the oxygen sensor voltage is abnormal and stores P0136/29 or P0156/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.
Open or short in oxygen sensor circuit
During active air-fuel ratio control, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition.

If the oxygen sensor output voltage is 0.21V or less (lean) even though the active air-fuel ratio control target is rich, the engine control computer judges that there is a malfunction in the oxygen sensor circuit and stores P0137/29 or P0157/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.

If the oxygen sensor output voltage is 0.59V or more (rich) even though the active air-fuel ratio control target is lean, the engine control computer judges that there is a malfunction in the oxygen sensor circuit and stores P0138/29 or P0158/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.

If the oxygen sensor output voltage remains 1.2V or more for 10 seconds or more, the engine control computer judges that there is a malfunction in the oxygen sensor circuit and stores P0138/29 or P0158/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.
When all of the following conditions are met
Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher
Throttle valve is not fully closed
Air-fuel ratio feedback control in progress
Fuel cut is not being performed
Same as P0136/29, P0156/27 (oxygen sensor voltage malfunction)
Same as P0136/29, P0156/27 (oxygen sensor voltage malfunction)

When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.3 or less (rich target), the oxygen sensor output voltage stays only between 0.21V and 0.59V.
When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.9 or more (lean target), the oxygen sensor output voltage stays only between 0.21V and 0.59V.
When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.3 or less (rich target), the oxygen sensor output voltage is less than 0.21 V
